0.original: <hex:024804F201FC03><hex:024904F201FD03> Quest Sync<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103><hex:02100103>The electrope enthusiast is scrutinizing the machinery.

24.original: Speak with the electrope enthusiast and have him accompany you.

25.original: Accompany the electrope enthusiast to the power converter and then speak with him.

26.original: Accompany the electrope enthusiast to the partitioned water tank and then speak with him.

27.original: Accompany the electrope enthusiast to the control tower and then speak with him.

28.original: Speak with the electrope enthusiast once more.

48.original: Well, if it isn't Her Majesty's special guest! Did our electrocapacitor catch your eye?

49.original: The machines here run on electrope, so the capacitor serves as a battery, storing the lightning energy as it rolls in from all the pylons we've erected.

50.original: If you're interested, I'd be happy to show you around and tell you more about our system!

51.original: Piqued your curiosity, eh? First, let's head downstairs to see the power converter!

52.original: The electrope enthusiast is now accompanying you. Keep him at your side in order to proceed with quest objectives.

53.original: You can leave the electrope enthusiast behind by entering a different area, or by speaking with him and selecting the option to part ways.

54.original: If you wish to have the electrope enthusiast join you again, return and speak with him at the original location.

57.original: Part ways with the electrope enthusiast.

59.original: It's great to see folks taking an interest in electrope. Any excuse to talk about it is always welcome!

60.original: Are you sure you wish to part ways with the electrope enthusiast?

61.original: Something came up, I take it? Another time, then! If you need to find me, I'll be near the electrocapacitor.

62.original: Welcome back! Now, where were we?

64.original: That's our food storage facility. By converting lightning energy to ice, we've created a refrigeration system that can prevent spoilage.

65.original: It's a godssend, I'll tell you that. These parts get a lot of rain and humidity, so if we didn't have refrigeration, we'd have a massive mold problem on our hands.

66.original: After lightning energy is absorbed in the electrocapacitor, it's transmitted to this power converter.

67.original: Its function is to stabilize and distribute appropriate levels of energy to each household and facility.

68.original: ...You look lost. Are you more of a visual learner? Let's pay a visit to the partitioned water tank on the north side of town.

69.original: Right, so, after lightning energy is allocated to the residential grid, it's utilized in a variety of ways, one of which is that tank there.

70.original: Normally, it's a receptacle for filtering rainwater. By using electrope to convert the lightning energy to fire, however, we can have hot water readily available at any time!

71.original: Amazing, isn't it? Lastly, let's go and have a look at the control tower just up the stairs.

72.original: These panels enable us to freely adjust each of the public utilities individually.

73.original: The utility manager monitors the operational status of each facility, keeping an eye out for any problems. Not a glamorous job, but it's important work.

74.original: Well, I think that about covers it! Let's loop back around to the electrocapacitor, shall we?

75.original: So, how'd I do? Hopefully I've answered all your most burning questions.

76.original: Believe it or not, I'm not actually an engineer─just an apprentice. I was inspecting the capacitor when you arrived.

77.original: Thanks for letting me ramble, though. It was a great opportunity to brush up on my studies!
